notes: Mezo Mainnet (chain 31612). The `contracts.*` slots are intentionally null until adapters are deployed because the manifest's slot names — MockGaugeController, MockMatchbox, MockVeMezo — are also TYPES. Consumers (`packages/app/lib/contracts.ts`, `useVeMezoPosition`, `useGaugeData`, `MezoYieldOptimizer.castOptimalVote`) read them via `IGaugeController` / `IMatchbox` / `IVeMezo` ABIs. The real Mezo equivalents below in `external` use DIFFERENT ABIs: `MezoBoostVoter` is Solidly-derived (`pools()`, `vote(tokenId, pools, weights)`); `VeMEZO` is ERC-721 (`balanceOf` returns NFT count, not 18-decimal voting power). Wiring the real addresses directly into the mock slots would build cleanly but revert at runtime. The path to populating these slots requires (1) a `BoostVoterAdapter` that translates `IGaugeController` calls into `BoostVoter` calls, (2) a `MatchboxAdapter` that multiplexes per-gauge `BribeVotingReward` claims, (3) a `VeMezoVotingPower` shim that reads voting power across a user's NFT positions. Phase 3 of the mainnet rollout deploys those adapters and writes their addresses here. Phase 5 then deploys `MezoYieldOptimizer` against them and writes its address. The fail-fast in `contracts.ts` blocks mainnet builds until all four slots are populated.
